'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of New Zealand]]
**[[New Zealand]] [[Prime Minister of New Zealand|prime minister]] [[Christopher Luxon]] announces that holders of [[Immigrant investor programs|investor residence visas]] may buy or build a single [[Housing in New Zealand|home]] valued above {{FXConvert|NZL|{{#expr:5000000}}|cursign=[[New Zealand dollar|NZ$]]}}, following changes to the [[Visa policy of New Zealand|visa rules]] previously preventing such investments. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/new-zealand-allow-some-foreign-investors-buy-homes-2025-09-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Economy of South Korea]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy|trade ministry]] reports that [[Semiconductor industry in South Korea|semiconductor exports]] reached a record [[South Korean won|₩]]21 trillion (US$15 billion) in August, up nearly one-third from last year, contributing to total monthly exports of ₩81 trillion ($58.4 billion). [https://www.barrons.com/news/s-korea-posts-record-semiconductor-exports-in-august-b5d59a59 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–Nauru relations]]
**[[Australian prime minister]] [[Anthony Albanese]] announces that [[Australia]] will pay [[Nauru]] to accept foreign-born criminals who are expelled from Australia following the signing of a memorandum by [[President of Nauru|Nauruan president]] [[David Adeang]]. [https://apnews.com/article/australia-nauru-criminals-deportations-5660a662c7587bd251bca88f6046122a (AP)]
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**The [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|South Korean defense ministry]] announces that it has suspended the "Voice of Freedom" [[military radio]] broadcast to [[North Korea]] for the first time in 15 years as part of measures to reduce tensions between the two countries. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-suspends-anti-north-korea-radio-broadcasts-2025-09-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[August 2025 Indonesian protests]]
**The [[Commission for Missing Persons and Victims of Violence]] reports that 20 people are missing across [[Bandung]] and [[Depok]], [[West Java]], and the [[Jakarta metropolitan area]], [[Indonesia]], following the protests. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250902-20-people-missing-after-deadly-indonesia-protests (AFP via France 24)]
**[[Indonesian National Police|Police]] storm into the campuses of [[Universitas Pasundan]] and [[Universitas Islam Bandung]] in West Java, firing [[tear gas]] at protesters. [https://jabar.idntimes.com/news/jawa-barat/polisi-berondong-kampus-unpas-dan-unisba-dengan-gas-air-mata-00-9y7yl-vrpmnn (''IDN Times'')]
*[[Indonesia–Peru relations]]
**An Indonesian diplomat attached to the [[List of diplomatic missions of Indonesia|embassy]] in [[Lima]], [[Peru]], is shot dead by an unknown assailant. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Peru)|Peruvian foreign ministry]] opens an investigation into the shooting as the country sees a rise in [[extortion]] and [[homicide]]. [https://apnews.com/article/peru-shooting-indonesia-diplomat-boluarte-crime-54ef403f19d3639ed99aa965bc8d11a8 (AP)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in Burkina Faso]]
**[[Burkina Faso]] passes a law [[criminalization of homosexuality|criminalizing]] [[homosexuality]], providing sentences of between two and five years in prison as well as fines. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20250902-burkina-faso-s-junta-passes-law-banning-homosexuality (France 24)]
*An [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[Judiciary of Argentina|federal judge]] bars [[Mass media in Argentina|media outlets]] from publishing audio recordings made inside the [[Casa Rosada|presidential palace]], which reportedly include conversations involving [[President of Argentina|President]] [[Javier Milei]]'s sister and [[General Secretariat of the Presidency|chief of staff]], [[Karina Milei]], amid ongoing [[Corruption in Argentina|corruption]] allegations against [[Presidency of Javier Milei|the government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/argentina-federal-judge-bars-publication-audios-attributed-mileis-sister-2025-09-01/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Finland|Finnish]] [[Judicial system of Finland|court]] sentences [[Biafra]]n activist [[Simon Ekpa]] to six years in prison for [[incitement]], [[tax fraud]], and [[Terrorism in Finland|terrorism]], among other charges. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-finland-separatist-ekpa-d298d311058b4ae9261817bb346967c4 (AP)]

**[[Benin]]'s ruling coalition, composed of the [[Progressive Union Renewal]] and the [[Republican Bloc]], nominates [[Ministry of Economy and Finance (Benin)|finance minister]] [[Romuald Wadagni]] as their [[President of Benin|presidential]] candidate in the upcoming [[Elections in Benin|election]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/aug/30/guyana-presidential-election-irfaan-ali-oil (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines (2024–2025)|Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**The [[Philippine]] [[Senate Blue Ribbon Committee]] orders the arrest of two [[contractors]] who failed to attend hearings on alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] in [[flood control]] projects, as part of its probe into incomplete or substandard works awarded under [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Bongbong Marcos]]'s [[Build Better More|infrastructure program]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/philippines/philippines-arrest-of-no-show-contractors-in-flood-control-probe-ordered-1.500252227 (''Gulf News'')]

[https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ghanas-president-removes-countrys-chief-justice-after-investigation-2025-09-01/ (Reuters)]
